editorial.summary: A 2014 conversation about creative independence, public speech, work, health, money, sex, race and the consequences of turning private provocation into a broadcast. David Choe begins with Hong Dynasty and the prior proposed MMA fight, then recounts making Steve Lee wrestle for continued employment, filming paid-sex travel in Macau, diabetes and heavy-metal fears, disordered eating, Critter's training and injury, Regenokine and Asian-American male representation. Choe and Joe Rogan compare adolescent drawing, watercolor, publishing, television crews and independent media before tracing Choe's commercial-art experience on Vertical Limit and 28 Days. The second half covers Thumbs Up in Detroit, gambling treatment, private sexual and financial negotiations and an extended response to the DVDASA sexual-violence controversy. Choe denies the underlying event happened as narrated, says he exaggerated, accepts responsibility for publishing a story that sounded horrible, apologizes in part and also minimizes; Rogan states he cannot know the underlying fact and explains why listeners understood the account as assault. A separate Las Vegas story contains Steve Lee's direct refusal before Choe reports touching him; it is not absorbed into the earlier controversy. The episode closes with DVDASA production, doxxing, an unmade deceptive Girlfriend Experience proposal, the 2012 Reddit AMA, creative misery, sex-work/labor claims, han and ethnic essentialism, stand-up experiments and Bobby Lee recollections. Every explicit, offensive, contradictory and self-critical idea remains. Corrections, factual context, privacy, consent, medical caution and publication restrictions are separate metadata. No named line-level turns are published.
